buildcraftcore/item/gear_wood:
In your efforts to create simple automation you have found a useful part: a turnable gear!
Its only made of wood so it must be upgraded for more demanding tasks...
The Wooden Gear is the first crafting step when entering BuildCraft and is used as the base of a lot of things.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Craft Wood Gears in planned batches. Higher-tier gears consume the previous tier, so keep a few lower-tier spares for machines and tools.
buildcraftcore/item/gear_stone:
Wood has proven tough to use in proper machines so you decide to make a new gear out of stone.
As an added bonus it doesn't catch fire at all.
The Stone Gear is basically an upgrade of the Wooden Gear, used to make stronger machines due to the hardness of stone.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Craft Stone Gears in planned batches. Higher-tier gears consume the previous tier, so keep a few lower-tier spares for machines and tools.
buildcraftcore/item/gear_iron:
Stone has proven to be useful for simple machines, but doesn't hold up very well under the high stresses and temperatures found in engines and complex machinery.
Iron however is much better at these more demanding tasks.
Upgrading your gears again allows you to obtain more complex machinery due to the nature of the metal.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Craft Iron Gears in planned batches. Higher-tier gears consume the previous tier, so keep a few lower-tier spares for machines and tools.
buildcraftcore/item/gear_gold:
More complex tasks require lots of very small interlocking gears, and iron gears break easily when used in this fashion.
Gold never breaks when crafted into tiny gears, which allows it to be used for complex mechanisms.
The Gold Gear is the next tier of gear which is used by machines which work over a large areas.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Craft Gold Gears in planned batches. Higher-tier gears consume the previous tier, so keep a few lower-tier spares for machines and tools.
buildcraftcore/item/gear_diamond:
Within your deep mining excavations, you discover the rarest but strongest material of them all: diamonds.
Due to its strength, diamond gears allows for the most demanding of tasks to be completed without breaking down or wearing out the gears.
The final tier of gear, The Diamond Gear is the strongest gear which is required for the most complex of machines.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Craft Diamond Gears in planned batches. Higher-tier gears consume the previous tier, so keep a few lower-tier spares for machines and tools.
buildcraftcore/item/wrench: Machines are much easier to live with when rotating one does not require a pickaxe and a complete reinstallation.
The BuildCraft Wrench rotates and reconfigures supported machines, directional pipes and other BuildCraft blocks.

Hint: By default, items in the common c:tools/wrench tag can perform the same BuildCraft wrench interactions. Server packs can disable tag-based compatibility with useWrenchTag; BuildCraft wrench implementations remain supported.
buildcraftcore/item/paintbrush:
While the amount of splash and colour that is found around the world is quite amazing, imagine being able to change the color of certain blocks in world with a simple stroke.
While painting blocks for decoration is nice, it can also have a practical use such as separating pipes.

Paintbrushes can be used to paint various different blocks into one of 16 colours.
Painting a block is normally only useful for decoration, however some blocks have special properties once painted.
For example pipes will not connect to other pipes if they are painted different colours.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Keep separate brushes for permanent pipe networks. Colouring only the branches that must not connect is usually easier to maintain than colouring every pipe.
buildcraftcore/item/marker_connector: Large work areas become much easier to manage when their laser boxes can be adjusted without rebuilding every marker.
The Marker Connector links compatible markers and directly edits Volume Box and Path Marker geometry.
Hint: Connections are still limited by the Core markerMaxDistance setting, so a marker that looks aligned may simply be too far away to link.

Use the Marker Connector on a visible laser box to begin adjusting it, move the cursor to the desired position, then use the connector again to finish. Sneak-use on a laser box removes that box. It can also link Path Markers in travel order and connect area markers that are within the configured reach.
buildcraftcore/item/marker_path: Straight lines are useful, but large projects often need a route that bends around terrain and machinery.
Path Marks define an ordered route for machines that support path-based work.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Place Path Markers in travel order and keep each segment unobstructed. A short test path is useful before assigning robots or automated builders to it.

Place Path Marks at the points the route should pass through. Use the Marker Connector to link them in order. The visible laser line shows the path that a compatible Builder or other machine will follow.

A path is directional: the order in which marks are linked determines the order of the points. Break or reconnect marks to reshape the route.
Place a compatible machine next to one of the linked Path Marks. The machine reads the whole connected route and repeats its work at each position along that path.
buildcraftcore/item/list: Nine filter slots are not much help when a sorting system must recognise an entire workshop of related materials.
A List stores reusable item filters for pipes, gates and robot stations.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Use Lists for reusable filters shared by several Diamond Pipes or gates. Updating one List is safer than editing many individual filter slots.

Hold the List and right-click to open it. Give the list a name, place reference items into the phantom slots and choose how each entry should be matched.

Exact matching keeps item data and other relevant details. Broader modes can match related item types or materials when supported by the current item registry.

Place the configured List into a parameter or filter slot that accepts it. The receiving pipe, gate or robot action treats the entries as one reusable filter. The List is not consumed when used as a filter.
buildcraftcore/block/engine_wood: In a quest to create power, you have discovered a way to produce a small amount of power using just a redstone signal.
The Redstone Engine is the smallest BuildCraft MJ engine. It needs only a redstone signal and produces 0.05 MJ per tick.
<bold>Hint:</bold> A Redstone Engine is best used for low-demand extraction and simple devices. It cannot replace a stronger engine when a machine has a meaningful MJ requirement.
Its output is 0.05 MJ/t. That is enough for light-duty direct consumers and extraction helpers, but it is intentionally unable to drive a Kinesis/Power Pipe network as a normal generator.

Normal BuildCraft engine heat uses the stages Blue, Green, Yellow, Red and <bold>Overheat</bold>. The Black stage is reserved for the Creative Engine rather than being a normal hottest heat stage. The Redstone Engine self-regulates below Overheat and cannot explode from heat.
It only connects to compatible direct MJ consumers and does not connect to Kinesis/Power Pipes. Use a Wrench to rotate the engine so its moving end faces the device it should power.

As with all engines, it <bold>requires a redstone signal to run.</bold> Gates can detect engine temperature stages and are useful for automatic control. Rate readouts may appear per tick or per second depending on the Core display setting.

buildcraftenergy/block/engine_stone: A furnace that moves a piston instead of cooking dinner is still a perfectly respectable furnace.
The Stirling Engine burns ordinary furnace fuels and produces between roughly 0.33 and 1 MJ per tick. In automatic FE compatibility modes that output may also feed compatible FE consumers.

Hint: Leave a way to disable a Stirling Engine when its consumer stops. By default overheating stops generation without an explosion; servers can enable destructive Stirling overheating with engines.stirlingExplosion.

Place any valid furnace fuel in the engine's single fuel slot and supply a redstone signal. The engine adjusts its output between roughly 0.33 MJ/t and 1 MJ/t according to the amount of MJ already held in its 1,000 MJ internal buffer.

The engine consumes the same furnace fuels recognised by Minecraft. Containers returned by a fuel, such as an empty bucket, remain available through the engine inventory. The guide uses per-tick rates; the live GUI may show per-second values when that display mode is enabled.

Place the engine against an MJ receiver. It selects a compatible output face when placed; use a Wrench to rotate it when another face should be powered. The normal heat stages are blue, green, yellow, red and overheat; Black is reserved for the Creative Engine. Stirling heat follows the fill level of its 1,000 MJ power buffer. If output is blocked, the buffer fills and the engine eventually reaches Overheat, where it stops generating until stored MJ can leave and the engine cools. The common setting engines.stirlingExplosion defaults to false; when enabled, reaching Overheat can instead destroy the engine in an explosion. When Core power mode is MJ_AUTOCONVERT_FE or DISPLAY_FE, normal engine compatibility may expose this MJ output to FE consumers using the configured MJ/FE ratio. Dedicated FE conversion is available separately through the FE Engine and MJ Dynamo.
buildcraftenergy/block/engine_iron: Refining oil is useful. Turning it into enough power to run an industrial accident is considerably more useful.
The Combustion Engine burns BuildCraft liquid fuels, uses coolant to control heat and stores residue produced by dirty fuels.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Provide reliable cooling and an automatic shutdown condition before leaving a Combustion Engine unattended. Test the complete fuel and coolant supply under full load.

The engine has separate tanks for fuel, coolant and residue. Fluid pipes or containers can fill and drain them directly. Apply a redstone signal to burn the inserted fuel; output depends on the selected fuel and ranges from low-output oil products to 8 MJ/t Gaseous Fuel.

Crude Oil, Heavy Oil and Dense Oil are dirty fuels. Burning them gradually produces Residue, and a full residue tank prevents that by-product from being accepted. Refined fuels burn without residue. The guide uses per-tick rates; the live GUI may display the equivalent per-second rate.

Water is the standard liquid coolant. Ice and Packed Ice can also be loaded as solid coolants and are converted into water with greater cooling strength. Hot biomes make the engine heat faster and cool less efficiently, while cold biomes have the opposite effect.

When the redstone signal is removed the engine pauses, applies a short restart cooling penalty and begins shedding excess heat. Keep coolant supplied before operating high-output fuels for long periods.

Place the engine against an MJ receiver and rotate it with a Wrench when necessary. The coloured stages show its heat level. Stored MJ is transferred only when the adjacent receiver accepts it; unaccepted power remains in the engine rather than being removed twice.

Automatic FE compatibility, when enabled in Core power mode, can expose compatible engine output to FE consumers at the configured conversion ratio. The FE Engine and MJ Dynamo remain the explicit conversion blocks when you want the boundary to be visible.
buildcraftfactory/block/distiller: Crude oil is a complicated collection of useful fluids waiting for someone to separate them.
The Distiller consumes MJ and separates a fluid into one gaseous output and one liquid output.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Store each Distiller output in a separate tank. Mixing intermediate fluids or routing both outputs through one unfiltered line makes later refining stages difficult to diagnose.

Insert the source fluid into the input tank. The gaseous product is extracted from the top and the liquid product from the bottom. Keep both outputs clear: the machine cannot complete another operation when either destination has no room.

Supply MJ through a compatible power connection. More available power lets the current operation advance faster, up to the machine's processing limit.

Cool, Hot and Searing forms of the same oil product can have different distillation recipes. The outputs retain the input temperature, so a Heat Exchanger is used between distillation stages when the next recipe requires another heat level.

Crude Oil can begin three different refining routes. Further distillation of Distilled Oil, Heavy Oil, Dense Oil and the mixed fuels separates them into Gaseous, Light and Dense Fuel plus Residue.
buildcraftfactory/block/heat_exchange: Some recipes require patience, others require the feedstock to be considerably hotter first.
The Heat Exchanger moves heat between two fluid streams and converts BuildCraft fluids between Cool, Hot and Searing states.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Use dedicated hot and cold fluid lines around a Heat Exchanger. Short, clearly labelled loops make temperature mistakes easier to find.

A Heat Exchanger consists of a start, one or more middle sections and an end connected in a straight line. Up to three middle sections can be used; additional valid sections increase the amount processed by the assembled machine.

Feed a heatable fluid into the heating side and a coolable fluid into the cooling side. Heat is transferred rather than created for free: one stream becomes hotter while the other becomes cooler. BuildCraft oil products move through Cool, Hot and Searing states in ten millibucket recipe units.

Water can absorb heat, while Lava can supply it. Fluid direction and available output space determine whether the exchanger can continue processing.

The selected temperature matters to the Distiller, so route fluids through the Heat Exchanger before the next refining stage when necessary.

The tank is a way to directly store fluids without the need for buckets and chests.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Leave access to at least one face of a tank column for inspection and emergency draining. Separate unrelated fluids into visibly separate banks.
Tanks can be used to store up to 16 buckets of one fluid per tank block and the tanks can be stacked vertically indefinitely to form one large tank.

Breaking a Tank does not keep the fluid inside the tank item itself. Instead, its stored fluid is converted into <bold>Fragile Fluid Shards</bold> so the fluid can be recovered and moved into another compatible tank or machine. A vertical tank column still stores up to 16 buckets per tank block.
buildcraftfactory/block/pump: The collection of fluids by hand can be tedious, dangerous and very bad for shoes.
The Pump finds a connected fluid body below itself, drains it in a controlled order and outputs the collected fluid to adjacent tanks or pipes.
Hint: For oceans and other renewable water sources, check the pumpsConsumeWater setting before assuming the Pump will reshape the terrain.

Place a Pump above the target fluid and supply MJ. Its tube searches downward until it reaches a fluid, then scans the connected fluid body incrementally instead of trying to process an entire ocean in one server tick. pumpMaxDistance limits how far the connected-fluid scan may travel from its target fluid position in any direction: the default is 64 blocks and the configurable range is 16 to 128. Unloaded chunks are not pulled in merely to continue the scan. Collected fluid is automatically offered to adjacent fluid handlers.

By default pumpsConsumeWater is false. When the Pump recognises a vanilla-style infinite water source it keeps the renewable source in place while still producing water. Enable that option when using finite-water behaviour and the Pump will drain water normally. Other fluids are drained from the world as usual. More available MJ increases work speed up to the machine limit. A redstone signal pauses the Pump.
buildcraftfactory/block/flood_gate: Buckets are excellent for one hole. They become less charming when the hole is an artificial lake.
The Flood Gate accepts fluid and places full source blocks into reachable empty space without consuming MJ.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Test a Flood Gate in a contained basin first. Its search can reach far beyond the block itself, so open only the sides that should seed the fill.

Pipe fluid into the Flood Gate and configure its open faces. It keeps a two-bucket internal tank and places one bucket at a time into reachable positions. A redstone signal pauses placement. Normal liquids search downward and sideways; lighter-than-air fluids search upward and sideways.

The current search radius is 64 blocks. The scan is performed incrementally and is bounded so a very large cavern cannot monopolise one server tick. The gate prefers connected reachable space rather than teleporting fluid through sealed blocks.
buildcraftfactory/block/mining_well: Sometimes the shortest route to a resource is still a perfectly vertical hole.
The Mining Well digs a single column below itself, places its tube through the shaft and outputs the drops it can legally mine.
<bold>Hint:</bold> A Mining Well stops at unbreakable or otherwise invalid obstacles. Use it for narrow probes; use a Quarry when the useful area is wider than one column.

The Mining Well searches straight down from its block position and mines breakable blocks using the machine owner identity. Drops are offered to adjacent inventories and item transport; if nothing accepts them they may be ejected into the world. Water in the shaft can be skipped, while an unbreakable block or unsuitable obstructing fluid stops further progress.

Supply MJ to mine. Harder blocks require more energy to break. The maximum vertical search is controlled by the Core miningMaxDepth setting and the actual world build-height limits, so modern worlds are not described simply as “digging to bedrock”. A redstone signal pauses the machine.
buildcraftfactory/block/chute: While a basic hopper is nice, it isn't very functional or original.
The Chute is similar to the hopper, but with more functionality.

<bold>Hint:</bold> The facing side is the pickup side; the other five sides are outputs. Point the Chute upward for slow gravity-assisted pickup without external MJ, or supply MJ when another pickup direction is required.

The Chute is a small transfer inventory. It pulls loose item entities through its <bold>facing side</bold>, then tries to send stored items to inventories, entities and pipes on the other five sides. The pickup face itself is not used as an output.

Each pickup cycle requires work. When the Chute faces upward it receives a small amount of free gravity progress, so it can collect items above itself slowly without external power. MJ accelerates that progress, and Chutes facing any other pickup direction need MJ to collect loose items. A Redstone Engine is sufficient for light-duty use.
buildcraftfactory/block/auto_workbench: As with every engineer's duty, you eventually find a reason to automate the crafting table as well.
The Auto Workbench stores a recipe, accepts ingredients from automation and crafts it repeatedly. It works slowly by itself and can use MJ to accelerate progress.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Buffer both ingredients and outputs around an Auto Workbench. External MJ is most useful when the recipe already has a reliable ingredient supply.

Set the phantom recipe in the grid, then insert or pipe in matching ingredients. The workbench balances its material slots around the ingredients the current recipe needs and exposes the crafted result through its output slot. The Recipe Book can fill the phantom grid directly without consuming ingredients.

If several recipes match the same phantom grid, left-click the recipe output selector for the next recipe or right-click for the previous one; the choice is saved.

A craft requires 40 MJ of progress. Without external power the workbench generates 0.2 MJ/t internally, so an uninterrupted craft takes about ten seconds. It also accepts MJ directly and can therefore complete that progress faster. If the recipe becomes invalid, stored progress decays instead of being kept forever. In automatic FE compatibility modes the normal MJ receiver may also be supplied through FE conversion.
buildcraftlib/config/registry_overview: The guide registry is the table of contents behind the book: it decides what exists, where it appears and which icon represents it.
This page describes the language-neutral Guide Book manifest used by BuildCraft Community Edition.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Keep page IDs stable after release; changing the display text is safe, while changing an ID can invalidate saved book history and external links.
Every entry has an id and a language-neutral page key. Optional fields define module, type, subtype, display-name fallback, book, listing state, item stack, NBT variant, statement and required mod.

The built-in manifest never contains translated prose. Page mechanics live in page_layouts.json; English and translated strings live in the files under text/. Resource packs can replace those built-in layers independently, while addons can contribute sections, entries and pages through Guide API2 without replacing BuildCraft resources.
Every manifest page key must exist in the shared layouts and in the default English text pack. Translations may omit pages or individual slots when a fallback is configured.
buildcraftlib/config/json_insn_format: Data-driven instructions are useful when a resource pack must adjust a registry without compiling Java code.
This technical page summarizes the legacy BuildCraft JSON instruction language retained for resource compatibility.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Prefer the packed manifest and text resources for new Guide Book pages; use instruction scripts only when modifying a legacy registry script.
Instruction files start with the marker below. Imported library files use ~{buildcraft/json/lib} instead and may declare an argument count with ~args N.
The parser accepts comments and function calls such as add, remove, replace, modify, overwrite, alias and import. Arguments may be numbers, quoted strings or backtick-delimited multi-line strings.

The Community Edition guide no longer loads one Markdown file per entry. Index metadata is in original_manifest.json, shared templates are in page_layouts.json, and translated slot arrays are in text/<language>.json.
buildcraftlib/config/guide_page_format: A guide page stays maintainable when mechanics and translations are not copied into every language.
This page describes the packed, localized Guide Book resource format used by BuildCraft Community Edition.
<bold>Hint:</bold> After changing a layout, test both Lore and Hints settings and open the page in English and at least one translated language.

Language-neutral page structure is stored once in assets/buildcraft/guide/page_layouts.json. Each page has a Markdown template and numbered {{bc_text:index}} slots. Recipes, links, images, visibility tags and other mechanics belong in the template.

Visible text is stored in one compact file per language under assets/buildcraft/guide/text/<language>.json. A page value is an array whose indexes match the template slots. This keeps technical structure out of translations and lets the whole language compress as one JAR entry.

assets/buildcraft/guide/languages.json selects the default language, regional aliases and fallback chains. A missing page or a null slot inherits its parent language; an empty string intentionally hides that slot.

original_manifest.json contains the built-in index metadata: page ID, page key, module, type, subtype, visibility and optional item or statement references. The page key connects an entry to its layout and localized text. Addons do not need to replace this file: Guide API2 sections and entries are merged into the same runtime contents and search index.
Normal Markdown text, headings and formatting tags are supported. The tags below are language-neutral and should remain in the shared layout.
buildcraftsilicon/item/plug_facade: Do pipes not match the theme of your build? Just place a facade of a block to match your build to hide them away
A Facade is a pluggable which is used to cover your pipes to match your build.

Hint: Facades are enabled by default. Servers can disable creation and placement of new facades with facades.enable; facades already placed in a world are preserved so existing builds are not corrupted.

Almost any supported block state can be made into a facade and placed on the side of a pipe. A solid Facade blocks a pipe connection through that face, while a Hollow Facade allows the connection to pass through. The common Silicon setting facades.enable defaults to true. When disabled, new facades cannot be placed or produced by the normal facade recipes/Assembly Table paths, but already installed facades continue to load and render.
buildcraftsilicon/item/plug_gate: Redstone takes up a lot of space nowadays. Why not have finer control over system in a more compact space using pipes. Just place a Gate on a pipe and start thinking.
The Gate is a upgradeable pluggable used to provide a logistical framework to help manage your pipe system.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Configure the pluggable before copying or installing many of them. Test one pipe face first to confirm orientation and gate interaction.

A Gate is a pluggable so it can only be placed on pipes and can be placed on any side of a pipe.
Any pipe placed next to it on that side will not connect.

Gates come in different tiers the provides a different amount of slots:
Basic Gate - Provides 1 set of slots (this cannot be modified).
Iron Gate - Provides 2 sets of slots.
Nether Brick Gate - Provides 4 sets of slots.
Gold Gate - Provides 8 sets of slots.

Gates can be modified to provide parameter slots:
Lapis Expansion - Provides 1 parameter slot to each trigger.
Quartz Expansion- Provides 1 parameter slot to each set (will cut the amount of slots the gate has by half).
Diamond Expansion- Provides 3 parameter slots to set (will cut the amount of slots the gate has by half).

Using an AND Gate ensures that </bold>all</bold> connected Triggers are active before the connection to the actions is made active.
Using an OR Gate ensures that </bold>one or more</bold> connected Triggers are active before the connection to the actions is made active.

The Icons on the left-hand side are known as Triggers. These are dragged into the slots on the left side of the GUI.
Different Triggers are used to detect different things, each with a different criteria. When a Triggers criteria is met, the adjacent connection will become active.

The Icons on the right-hand side are known as Actions. These are dragged into the slots on the right side of the GUI.
Different actions result in different task being completed. When the adjacent connection is active, the connected actions are undertaken.

When Parameter slots are installed, extra slots next to some triggers/actions become available. 
These extra slots can provide extra functionality to make your triggers/actions more specific.
In these extra slots you either: click the slot to access more options or place items in as a filter.

The lines down the middle are used to connect the Triggers to the Actions, so they can work together.
They can be clicked to be connected/disconnected to require multiple triggers/actions to require multiple triggers/actions etc.
When a trigger is met, the line in the middle will light up (only partially if there are multiple triggers required).
When a line is lit up, then the actions they are connected to will be undertaken.
buildcraftsilicon/item/plug_pulsar: Being able to power your pipes for free without needing a big engine? How cool is that!
<bold>Hint:</bold> Configure the pluggable before copying or installing many of them. Test one pipe face first to confirm orientation and gate interaction.
The Pipe Pulsar is a pluggable used to provide small amounts of power to power accepting pipes.

It can only be placed on any power accepting pipe and can be right-clicked to be activated.
The activation of a Pipe Pulsar can also be done with a Gate using Pulsar actions.

Pluggables can only be placed on pipes and can be placed on any side of a pipe.
It will stop any other pipe and pipe wire connection between two pipes when placed in between.
buildcraftsilicon/item/plug_light_sensor: Through a light sensor you can use the power of light to control your gates.
The Light Sensor is a pluggable used to detect the light level of the block in front of it and provide that data to the Gate on the adjacent side of the  same pipe.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Configure the pluggable before copying or installing many of them. Test one pipe face first to confirm orientation and gate interaction.

This data allows the adjacent Gate to detect whether it is light or dark through the Bright and Dark triggers.
These Bright and Dark triggers can be used to trigger an action through a Gate.

Pluggables can only be placed on pipes and can be placed on any side of a pipe.
It will stop any other pipe and pipe wire connection between two pipes when placed in between.
buildcraftsilicon/item/plug_lens: Signals are easier to understand when they are visible, and easier to control when they can be filtered.
Lenses and Filters are coloured pipe pluggables stored as variants of the same item.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Configure the pluggable before copying or installing many of them. Test one pipe face first to confirm orientation and gate interaction.
A Lens displays and projects its colour when the connected pipe-wire signal is active. Use it as a compact visual indicator on any free pipe side.

Filter variants use the same sixteen colours but act as statement parameters and pluggable filters where supported. Their colour and filter state are stored in the item variant, so copying only the base registry ID is not enough to identify a specific filter.
buildcraftsilicon/trigger/light_high: Is it light outside the gate? If so then it will trigger.
Bright is a gate trigger provided on any gate that also has a Light Sensor of that colour is attached to the same pipe.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Connect the trigger to a temporary lamp first. Once its active and inactive states are confirmed, route the same signal to machinery.
When selected, the connected actions will only be activated when the light level of the block in front of the Light Sensor is high.
buildcraftsilicon/trigger/light_low: Is it light outside the gate? If not then it will trigger.
Dark is a gate trigger provided on any gate that also has a Light Sensor of that colour is attached to the same pipe.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Connect the trigger to a temporary lamp first. Once its active and inactive states are confirmed, route the same signal to machinery.
When selected, the connected actions will only be activated when the light level of the block in front of the Light Sensor is low.
buildcraftsilicon/action/pulsar_constant: Did you know you can active control over a connected pipe pulsar using a gate?
Power Pulsar On is a gate action provided on any gate that also has a Pipe Pulsar is attached to the same pipe.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Pair this action with the narrowest useful trigger and test the off-state as carefully as the on-state.
When the action is activated, the Pipe Pulsar is activated and the pipe will receive power.

Gates may show the Power Pulsar action multiple times in different colours to represent each of the different connected Pipe Pulsars.
The colour of the action represents the direction of the Pipe Pulsar in relation of the pipe so you can differentiate between each Pipe Pulsar.
buildcraftsilicon/action/pulsar_single: Did you know you can make a connected pipe pulsar only pulse once?
Single Power Pulse is a gate action provided on any gate that also has a Pipe Pulsar is attached to the same pipe.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Pair this action with the narrowest useful trigger and test the off-state as carefully as the on-state.
When the action is activated, the Pipe Pulsar is activated for a short time and the pipe will receive enough power to complete one operation.

Gates may show the Power Pulsar action multiple times in different colours to represent each of the different connected Pipe Pulsars.
The colour of the action represents the direction of the Pipe Pulsar in relation of the pipe so you can differentiate between each Pipe Pulsar.
buildcrafttransport/pipe/structure: Want to transmit your pipe signals without stuff travelling through it. Just fill it up with gravel.
A Structure Pipe is a pipe which can carry gates/pipe wires but nothing can travel through it.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Structure Pipes are useful mounting points for wires, gates and plugs where no item transport is required.

Just like a normal pipe, Pluggables and Pipe Wires can be placed on it without carrying items, fluids, MJ or FE.

Pipe holders in current BuildCraft versions are waterloggable. A pipe placed into water can preserve the water in its block space instead of requiring the network to drain the area first. This applies to transport pipes as well as Structure Pipes.
buildcrafttransport/pipe/wood_item: Want to take items out and transport them somewhere else? Just give it power and watch it them flow.
A Wooden Transport Pipe is used to extract items from an inventory when given power.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Power extraction only when the destination network has somewhere to send the item. A nearby buffer prevents repeated ejection from a blocked line.

When powered, It will extract and transport the items to any other connecting inventories/pipes.
The extraction of items will occur out of solid side of the pipe and transport them towards the clear facing sides.
If it has multiple clear facing sides, the items will move randomly between them.
If there is no where for the items to go, the extracted items will drop out of the pipe onto the ground.

Some machines can automatically output items directly into a Wooden Transport Pipe without the pipe needing to be powered.
Using Pipe Plugs or painting pipes a different colour can stop pipes connecting.
It can receive power from any MJ power source such as: an engine, a power adaptor, or a pipe pulsar.

For each pulse of power it receives, it will extract items from the adjacent inventory.
The more power a pulse has, the more items will be extracted per pulse.
buildcrafttransport/pipe/cobble_item: Transporting items at a slow and steady pace to where you want them to go.
A Cobblestone Transport Pipe is used to transport items from a pipe into connecting pipes/inventories.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Use Cobblestone and Stone pipes together when adjacent lines must remain separate without paint or plugs.

The Cobblestone Transport pipe gives transported items a high amount of drag so they will slow accelerated items quickly.

Cobblestone Transport pipes will not connect to Stone or Quartz Transport Pipes.

If it has multiple connecting sides, the items will travel in a random direction.
Items will not travel back in the direction it came from and only go a different direction.
If there is no where for the travelling items to go, they will be dropped out of the pipe onto the ground.

Some machines can automatically output items directly into it without being fed through a powered extraction pipe.
Using Pipe Plugs or painting pipes a different colour can stop pipes connecting.
buildcrafttransport/pipe/stone_item: Transporting items at a medium pace to where you want them to go.
A Stone Transport Pipe is used to transport items from a pipe into connecting pipes/inventories.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Use Stone and Cobblestone pipes together when adjacent lines must remain separate without paint or plugs.

The Stone Transport pipe gives transported items a medium amount of drag so they will slow accelerated items.

Stone Transport pipes will not connect to Cobblestone or Quartz Transport Pipes.

If it has multiple connecting sides, the items will travel in a random direction.
Items will not travel back in the direction it came from and only go a different direction.
If there is no where for the travelling items to go, they will be dropped out of the pipe onto the ground.

Some machines can automatically output items directly into it without being fed through a powered extraction pipe.
Using Pipe Plugs or painting pipes a different colour can stop pipes connecting.
buildcrafttransport/pipe/quartz_item: Transporting items at a faster pace to where you want them to go.
A Quartz Transport Pipe is used to transport items from a pipe into connecting pipes/inventories.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Quartz pipes are convenient for visually distinct backbone routes. Keep specialised sorting close to branch points rather than along the whole trunk.

The Quartz Transport pipe gives transported items a small amount of drag so they will slow accelerated items.

Quartz Transport pipes will not connect to Cobblestone or Stone Transport Pipes.

If it has multiple connecting sides, the items will travel in a random direction.
Items will not travel back in the direction it came from and only go a different direction.
If there is no where for the travelling items to go, they will be dropped out of the pipe onto the ground.

Some machines can automatically output items directly into it without being fed through a powered extraction pipe.
Using Pipe Plugs or painting pipes a different colour can stop pipes connecting.
buildcrafttransport/pipe/iron_item: Want to transport your items in only one direction? Just set the pipes direction and pipe them through.
A Iron Transport Pipe is used to transport items from a pipe in one direction towards a connecting pipe/inventory.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Set the output direction with a Wrench after every rotation or relocation. A wrong arrow can create a silent dead end.

Items enter through the solid sides and leave through the clear output side. Change the output by using a Wrench on the side you want, or by using a Gate direction action. An ordinary redstone signal does <bold>not</bold> rotate the pipe.

Items do not immediately return through the side they entered from. If the selected output cannot accept them, travelling items keep retrying until a route becomes available. Some machines can also output items directly into the pipe.
buildcrafttransport/pipe/gold_item: Transporting items at a really fast pace to where you want them to go.
A Gold Transport Pipe is used to quickly transport them to connecting pipes/inventories.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Use Gold Pipes on long straight runs, then slow or buffer items before complex junctions where rapid bursts can overwhelm inventories.

The Gold Transport pipe gives transported items a large speed boost so they will travel around pipes faster.

If it has multiple connecting sides, the items will travel in a random direction.
Items will not travel back in the direction it came from and only go a different direction.
If there is no where for the travelling items to go, they will be dropped out of the pipe onto the ground.

Some machines can automatically output items directly into it without being fed through a powered extraction pipe.
Using Pipe Plugs or painting pipes a different colour can stop pipes connecting.
buildcrafttransport/pipe/diamond_item: Choosing which items can travel where might be useful for your system.
A Diamond Transport Pipe is used to transport items from a pipe in a direction set by its filter into either another adjacent pipe or inventory.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Leave an unfiltered side only when it is intended as overflow. Filtered sides take priority, so test scarce items before connecting bulk traffic.

The Diamond Transport Pipe has each of its sides distinguished by a different colour.
Opening up the Diamond Transport Pipe GUI will allow you to setup a filter.
Placing a items you want in a certain slots colour will allow you to filter which items can go in which direction.
Having multiple of the same items in a colour will allow you to add 'weight' to where you fluids will go.

A List can be used in a filtering slots to give you expanded filtering options.

In case of their being multiple directions items could go, the items will be distributed (depending of the weight you give them) between them.
Any valid direction with no filter set will allow any item to pass through but filtered directions will take priority.
Items will not travel back in the direction it came from and only in a different direction.
If there is no connecting pipe or the adjacent inventory is full and there is no where else for the item to go, the item will drop out of the pipe onto the ground.

Some machines can automatically output items directly into a Diamond Transport Pipe without needing to be fed through an extraction pipe.
Using Pipe Plugs or painting pipes a different colour can stop pipes connecting.
buildcrafttransport/pipe/obsidian_item: Picking up items from the world and moving them around is the future!
A Obsidian Transport Pipe is used to pick up in world items and transport them into a connecting pipe/inventory.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Power improves collection behaviour. Place the pipe where loose items cannot be pulled from areas that players still use manually.

Without MJ, loose items are collected only when they physically touch the pipe. When powered, the pipe searches outward from its open face. The powered search extends up to four blocks and widens with distance instead of using a fixed box above the pipe. More distant items require more MJ to pull in.

The Obsidian Transport Pipe needs exactly one pipe connection to collect items from the world. Its pickup face is the opposite, open side. With multiple pipe connections there is no single open face, so world-item collection is disabled.

If there is no where for the received items to go, they will be dropped out of the pipe onto the ground.
Using Pipe Plugs or painting pipes a different colour can stop pipes connecting.
It can receive power from any MJ power source such as: an engine, a power adaptor, or a pipe pulsar.

For each pulse of power it receives, it will pick up items from the ground.
The more power a pulse has, the more items will pick up per pulse.
buildcrafttransport/pipe/sandstone_item: Fed up of using pipe plugs? This pipe will only connect to pipes and nothing else.
A Sandstone Transport Pipe is used to transport items from a pipe into connecting pipes.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Sandstone Pipes are useful beside dense machine walls because they avoid unwanted inventory connections. Confirm every intended endpoint remains connected.

It does not connect to any machine so it only connects to other pipes.

If it has multiple connecting sides, the items will travel in a random direction.
Items will not travel back in the direction it came from and only go a different direction.
If there is no where for the travelling items to go, they will be dropped out of the pipe onto the ground.

Using Pipe Plugs or painting pipes a different colour can stop pipes connecting.
buildcrafttransport/pipe/clay_item: With the clay pipe, the items will never miss a chest ever again.
A Clay Transport Pipe is used to transport items from a pipe into a connecting pipes/inventories.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Use Clay Pipes at final delivery points where inventories should be preferred over continuing through the pipe network.

The Clay Transport pipe will prioritise trying to insert items into an inventory before traveling onwards.

If it has multiple connecting sides, the items will prioritise a connected inventory before travelling in a random direction.
Items will not travel back in the direction it came from and only go a different direction.
If there is no where for the travelling items to go, they will be dropped out of the pipe onto the ground.

Some machines can automatically output items directly into it without being fed through a powered extraction pipe.
Using Pipe Plugs or painting pipes a different colour can stop pipes connecting.
buildcrafttransport/pipe/void_item: When you transport items in, they wont come out.
A Void Transport Pipe is used to destroy items that are fed into it.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Place a filter before a Void Pipe whenever valuable and disposable items share a network. Never use the void route as an untested overflow.

Items can not travel through the pipe as any items that reach the centre are automatically destroyed.

Some machines can automatically output items directly into it without being fed through a powered extraction pipe.
Using Pipe Plugs or painting pipes a different colour can stop pipes connecting.
buildcrafttransport/pipe/stripes_item: Imagine a pipe which can place blocks, break blocks and use blocks. This is that pipe your imagining.
A Striped Transport Pipe is used to break blocks, place blocks use items fed through it and transport them into a connecting pipe/inventory.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Use Stripes Pipes at controlled endpoints and test the target face manually. Their world interaction is more destructive than normal transport.

When powered, It will break the block directly in front of it and pass it on to the adjacent pipe or inventory.
When a block is fed through it, It will place the block directly in front of it.
When an item is fed through it, It will attempt to 'use' it on the block/entity in front of it.

An Striped Transport Pipe has to be 'pointing' in a direction to effect the block in front of it.
With multiple pipes/inventories connected to it, It will lose its ability affect from the world.

If there is no where for the travelling items to go, they will be dropped out of the pipe onto the ground.
Using Pipe Plugs or painting pipes a different colour can stop pipes connecting.
It can receive power from any MJ power source such as: an engine, a power adaptor, or a pipe pulsar.

For each pulse of power it receives, it will use the power it received and attempt to break the block in front of it.
The more power a pulse has, the more power will be used to break the block.
buildcrafttransport/pipe/diamond_wood_it: Want to take certain items out and transport them somewhere else? Just give it power and watch them flow.
A Wooden Diamond Transport Pipe is used to extract selected items determined by its filter from an inventory when given power.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Configure the extraction filter before applying power. An empty or broad filter can drain an inventory much faster than expected.

When powered, It will extract the items selected in the filter and transport them to any other connected inventories/pipes.
The extraction of items will occur out of solid side of the pipe and transport them towards the clear facing sides.
If it has multiple clear facing sides, the items will move in a random direction.
If there is no where for the item to go, the extracted items will drop out of the pipe onto the ground.

Some machines can automatically output items directly into a Wooden Diamond Transport Pipe without the pipe needing to be powered (This will not respect the filter).
Using Pipe Plugs or painting pipes a different colour can stop pipes connecting.

Opening up the Wooden Diamond Transport Pipe GUI will allow you to setup a filter.
Placing items you want in the slots will allow you to filter what it extracts.
You can use the Whitelist, Blacklist or Round Robin options to change what your filter does:
Whitelist: Only the items selected will be extracted.
Blacklist: Any items other than the items selected will be extracted.
Round robin: Extracts the items in the exact order selected in the above filter slots (from left to right)

A List can be used in a filtering slots to give you expanded filtering options.
It can receive power from any MJ power source such as: an engine, a power adaptor, or a pipe pulsar.

For each pulse of power it receives, it will extract items from the adjacent inventory.
The more power a pulse has, the more items will be extracted per pulse.
buildcrafttransport/pipe/lapis_item: Want to your painted items, just set a colour and they will become that colour.
A Lazuli Transport Pipe is used to paint items and transport them to connected pipes/inventories.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Keep colour-based routing documented near the network. A paint change upstream can alter every later routing decision.

It will paint an item that travels through it to the colour set.
The colour it will paint the items can be changed by being whacked with a wrench or through a Gate.

If it has multiple clear facing sides, the items will move in a random direction.
Items will not travel back in the direction it came from and only go a different direction.

Some machines can automatically output items directly into it without being fed through a powered extraction pipe.

buildcrafttransport/pipe/daizuli_item: Want to sort your painted items, just set a colour and a direction and pipe them through.
A Daizuli Transport Pipe is used to transport send painted items it receives in one direction towards a connecting pipe/inventory.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Use Daizuli routing together with a clear colour convention. Reserve one colour for overflow or unsorted items.

Items will travel in through the solid sides and be fed out towards the clear facing side.
Items will not travel back in the direction it came from and only in a different direction.
If there is no where for the travelling items to go, they will be dropped out of the pipe onto the ground.

buildcraftcore/block/engine_basics: BuildCraft still runs on MJ, but modern factories often need to cross the boundary into Forge Energy as well.
BuildCraft uses MJ as its native machine and power-pipe energy. Dedicated FE machinery and an optional automatic conversion mode provide interoperability without replacing the MJ network.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Keep MJ and FE networks visually distinct until you know exactly where conversion happens. Dedicated converters make mixed-energy factories much easier to diagnose.

The default conversion is 1 MJ = 10 FE. It can be changed with the Core power.mjPerFe setting. MJ_ONLY is the default power mode: ordinary BuildCraft machines stay MJ-only, while the FE Engine, MJ Dynamo and FE Pipes remain available. MJ_AUTOCONVERT_FE additionally lets ordinary BuildCraft MJ machines accept FE and lets compatible engines feed FE consumers. DISPLAY_FE enables the same conversion behaviour and makes generic power readouts prefer FE.

This guide writes transfer rates per tick so different machines can be compared directly. The Core timeGap display setting can show live values per tick or per second instead; one second is twenty ticks, so 4 MJ/t is shown as 80 MJ/s when seconds are selected. Changing the display unit does not change machine speed or capacity.

Engines and converter engines require a redstone signal to work. Rotate directional machines with a Wrench so their working face points at the intended consumer. Back-pressure matters: when an internal buffer cannot empty, generation slows or stops and heat can rise. Use gates, storage or a shutdown signal instead of assuming unused power will disappear.

Sneak-use the Marker Connector on the box to remove it. Machines next to the box can use the selected volume in the same way as a Land Mark area.

buildcraftcore/item/marker_land: Large machines need an exact boundary, otherwise their appetite for blocks can become rather difficult to control.

<bold>Hint:</bold> Verify the coloured boundary lines from more than one side before starting a Quarry, Builder or Filler. One misplaced marker can select a much larger area than expected.

Place Land Marks on matching X, Y or Z axes and connect them with the Marker Connector. Connected marks form the edges of a rectangular box. Most machines only need the horizontal corners, but a full three-dimensional box may also be defined. Connections only search up to the configured markerMaxDistance on an axis. The default is 64 blocks and packs may configure it from 16 to 256. Powering a Land Mark with redstone displays guide lasers along the axes, making aligned placement easier.
Place the machine next to one of the connected marks. The machine claims the marked box and uses it as its work area. If no valid marks are found, some machines use their own default area instead.

Place the used Blueprint in a Builder. Supply the requested blocks, fluids and MJ. Persistent state that matters to supported blocks, such as non-decaying placed leaves, is retained when the schematic handler supports it.
buildcraftbuilders/item/template: Sometimes the shape matters more than the exact stone, wood or metal used to fill it.
A Template records only the occupied shape of an area, allowing a Builder to fill it with supplied materials.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Templates record shape rather than exact block identity. Use them when the same structure should be rebuilt from locally available materials.

Record a Template in an Architect Table exactly like a Blueprint. The scan remembers which positions are filled and which are empty, but does not preserve the original block types or block-entity data. Blank Templates stack to <bold>16</bold>; recorded Templates have a maximum stack size of <bold>1</bold>.

Insert the used Template into a Builder and supply the blocks you want to use. The Builder consumes available materials to reproduce the recorded shape. Templates are useful for roads, walls, shells and repeated structures where the final material may change.
buildcraftbuilders/item/schematic_single: Replacing every copy of one block in a large design by hand is a poor use of an architect's time.
A Single Block Schematic records one block state for use by the Replacer.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Single-block schematics are useful for testing placement rules and rotations before committing a large Blueprint to a Builder.

Use a blank schematic on a block to record it. The recorded schematic stores the block state and supported requirements needed to reproduce that block. Blank Single Block Schematics stack to <bold>16</bold>; a recorded schematic has a maximum stack size of <bold>1</bold>. Sneak-right-click to clear it, returning it to the blank stackable state.

The Replacer accepts a used Blueprint, a source schematic and a destination schematic. Every matching source block in the Blueprint is changed to the destination block without modifying the world directly.
buildcraftbuilders/item/filler_planner: A construction box is more useful when it remembers not only where to work, but what work should be done there.
The Filler Planner stores a Filler pattern and parameters as a Volume Box add-on.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Configure the attached planner through a Filler before supplying materials or MJ. The stored preview makes orientation mistakes easier to catch before the job runs.

Attach the planner to a Volume Box, then place a Filler so it uses that box. Open the Filler interface to configure the planner's pattern, parameters and inversion state; those settings are stored in the Volume Box add-on and are reused by a Filler attached to that box.

The preview is rendered around the Volume Box, making it possible to inspect the planned operation before committing materials and MJ.
buildcraftbuilders/block/architect: Before a machine can rebuild a structure, someone must first teach it what the structure is.
The Architect Table scans a marked area into a Blueprint or Template.

<bold>Hint:</bold> Scan a small representative structure first and test the resulting Blueprint in a safe area. Block entities, entities and special multi-block states are the parts most worth verifying before a large capture.
Place the table beside a connected Land Mark area or Volume Box. The selected box is read from the area provider behind or next to the table.

Insert a blank Blueprint to record exact blocks, states and supported data, or a blank Template to record only the shape. Choose whether the result may rotate, excavate existing blocks or use creative-only placement, then start the scan.

Scanning is incremental, so large areas take time rather than freezing the server. Keep the area loaded until the used snapshot appears in the output. The current Guide/tooltip UI does not provide a full 3D schematic preview; verify complex captures by testing the saved snapshot itself.
buildcraftbuilders/block/builder: A plan is only a collection of ideas until something begins placing blocks.
The Builder consumes MJ and resources to construct a used Blueprint or Template.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Keep spare output space while a Builder is active. If a task is cancelled, reserved items may return to its inventory or drop nearby when no slot is available.

Insert a used Blueprint or Template into the snapshot slot. The requirements display shows needed materials. Supply items through the resource inventory or connected item pipes, fluids through the internal tanks, and MJ through a compatible power connection.

Blueprints request their recorded blocks. Templates use suitable supplied blocks to reproduce the saved shape.

The structure is placed relative to the Builder's facing. Rotation and excavation are available only when allowed by the snapshot header. When a connected Path Mark route is present, the Builder can repeat the design at positions along the path.

World actions use the machine owner identity, so protected blocks and placement restrictions are checked instead of being silently bypassed. Work state and reserved resources are saved. After a reload, unfinished tasks are rechecked and reserved items, fluids and energy are safely returned before work resumes.
buildcraftbuilders/block/filler: Not every construction job needs a detailed Blueprint. Many jobs are simply boxes, walls, floors or a great deal of empty space.
The Filler applies a configurable geometric pattern inside a marked area.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Begin with a small marked area and a cheap material. Once the pattern and orientation are correct, move the same setup to the final site.

Place the Filler beside Land Marks or a Volume Box, then open its interface to refresh the work area. Supply building blocks to the resource slots and MJ to the internal battery. Placement treats normal replaceable blocks as valid targets instead of requiring literal air, while excavation patterns can remove existing blocks when excavation is enabled. World changes use the machine owner identity so protection rules can reject disallowed work.

Available patterns include clear, fill, box, frame, horizon, flatten, cylinder, pyramid and stairs. Two-dimensional shapes include triangles, regular polygons, arcs and circles. Three-dimensional shapes include spheres and partial spheres.

Pattern parameters control direction, rotation, facing, axis, centre and hollow variants. Inverting the selection swaps the inside and outside of the generated pattern.
buildcraftbuilders/block/library: A good design should survive longer than the one piece of paper on which it was first recorded.
The Electronic Library transfers Blueprint and Template data between snapshot items, the player's local blueprint library and the current world's machine storage.

<bold>Hint:</bold> Save important designs to the local blueprint library before taking snapshot items to a work site. The local library belongs to the client, while Builders and other machines use the current world's server-side copy; the two stores remain separate even in singleplayer.
Insert a used Blueprint or Template whose design exists in the current world's machine storage. After the transfer completes, the design is copied into the player's local blueprint library.

Select a stored design in the Library interface and insert a clean Blueprint or Template into the upload slot. The Library reuses the server-side copy when it already exists; otherwise it transfers the selected local snapshot to the current world's machine storage, then produces a used snapshot item.

Each transfer takes 50 ticks. Do not remove the input while its progress bar is moving.
buildcraftbuilders/block/replacer: Changing the material of a finished design should not require rebuilding the design from memory.
The Replacer changes every matching block in a used Blueprint from one recorded block state to another.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Test replacement rules on a small sample wall. Include every block state that matters, especially orientation and variants that look similar in inventory.

Place the used Blueprint in the Blueprint slot. Record the block to find in one Single Block Schematic and the replacement block in the other. The Replacer edits the Blueprint data and returns the modified design.

The machine changes the plan, not blocks already placed in the world. Both schematics are consumed by a completed replacement operation.
buildcraftbuilders/block/marker_construc: A Builder robot needs a plan and a place to collect work even when no stationary Builder is doing the construction itself.
The Construction Marker exposes Blueprint build tasks to Builder Robots.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Construction Markers are best used to inspect a plan before resources are supplied. Correct the anchor and orientation while changes are still free.

Place a Construction Marker and insert a used Blueprint. The marker creates build tasks but does not consume MJ or place blocks by itself. Nearby Builder Robots can reserve those tasks, fetch the required materials and perform the construction.

The marker uses the snapshot's rotation, excavation and ownership settings. Restrict Builder Robots with a work zone when several projects are close together.
buildcraftbuilders/block/frame: A large moving drill is much less alarming when it has a visible scaffold around its work area.
Frames are lightweight structural blocks used by the Quarry and construction systems.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Frames are temporary working blocks. Keep the construction area clear so machines can build and remove them without obstruction.

A Quarry automatically places Frames around its selected area before mining begins. The frame shows the working boundary and supports the moving drill assembly.

Frames may also be used as inexpensive open scaffolding, but a Quarry manages and removes its own frame blocks as part of its work cycle.
buildcraftbuilders/block/quarry: Mining by hand is rewarding until the desired ore is underneath several million blocks that are not the desired ore.
The Quarry builds a frame and automatically mines every permitted block inside its selected area.

<bold>Hint:</bold> Route Quarry output into a buffer or item pipe so mined drops do not spill onto the ground. A full output does not stop mining: anything that nearby inventories and pipes refuse is dropped beside the Quarry.

Place the Quarry beside connected Land Marks to define its horizontal work area. Without a valid marked area it creates a smaller default quarry in front of itself.

The Quarry can request chunk tickets for its work area when BuildCraft chunk loading is enabled and the configured chunk-loading level allows the machine. Server administrators can disable or restrict those tickets, so do not assume every server will keep a remote Quarry loaded automatically.

Supply MJ. The Quarry first scans and builds its frame, then moves the drill across the area and mines downward to the configured depth or world bottom. More available power allows more work to be completed each tick, up to the machine limit. Fluids and other non-mineable cells are handled without corrupting the frame or drill path.

Mined drops are offered to adjacent inventories and item pipes; anything left over is dropped into the world, so a blocked output does not halt the Quarry. Protected blocks are checked using the Quarry owner identity rather than silently bypassing normal player protection.

<bold>Warning:</bold> while clearing positions required for its own frame, the Quarry intentionally destroys obstructing blocks without keeping their drops. Keep valuable blocks, containers and machines out of the future frame line.

<bold>Hint:</bold> Start with one robot, two reachable Docking Stations and a small work zone. Expand only after charging, tool collection and unloading all work reliably.

Attach a Docking Station to a pipe, then use the programmed Robot on that station. The placing player becomes its owner. A station connected to MJ can recharge its docked robot.

Robots keep a safety energy reserve and return to a suitable station when they need to recharge, load or unload. Careers that break, place, use or attack perform those world interactions with the robot owner identity so normal protection systems can make the same access decision they would for that player. Gate actions on Docking Stations control filters, routes, work zones and which resources are available.
buildcraftrobotics/item/redstone_board: A machine can move, but without a board it has no idea whether it should carry, plant, mine or flee from the nearest cow.
A Redstone Board stores the career program installed into a Robot.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Store programmed boards by career in separate labelled inventories. Keeping an unprogrammed board nearby makes reconfiguration faster.

Place a blank board in a Programming Table, select a career and supply laser power. Blank boards stack to sixteen; programmed boards stack to one.

Programming costs depend on the career: basic logistics boards require 800 MJ, common work boards 3,200 MJ, advanced combat or delivery boards 12,800 MJ, and the Builder board 51,200 MJ.
Use an Integration Table to combine the programmed board with an empty Robot. Installing a board requires 5,000 MJ. The resulting Robot keeps that career until rebuilt with a different board.

A Docking Station is a pipe pluggable that links, charges and controls Robots.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Give every work area at least one station for charging and one clear route for loading or unloading. Station filters prevent robots from taking the wrong supplies.

Place the station on any free side of a pipe. Use a programmed Robot on the station to deploy it. A station can be occupied by only one robot at a time.

A pipe network carrying MJ can recharge the docked robot. Sneak-use a Wrench on a linked main station to release its robot back into item form when supported by the station state.

Attach a Gate to the pipe and use Robotics station actions to accept or provide items and fluids, request resources, forbid or force robots, and expose machine requests. Map Locations can restrict work or loading zones.
buildcraftrobotics/block/zone_planner: A robot told to work everywhere will eventually discover somewhere you did not want it to work.

<bold>Hint:</bold> Explore or otherwise load the terrain you want to paint before opening a large plan. The Zone Planner intentionally refuses to generate new chunks just to draw its map.

Insert a blank Map Location and edit the zone in the planner. The map supports sixteen independently editable layers over a 2048 by 2048 coordinate grid. Layers can be selected, combined and named in the interface.

Map data is read only from chunks that are already loaded/generated. Painting or importing a zone across unavailable terrain is clipped to the chunks the server can provide instead of force-generating new world data. After 120 ticks the output slot receives a Map Location containing the current Zone Plan; a saved zone may be placed in the import slot to continue editing it.
Place the resulting Map Location into a compatible Gate parameter or Docking Station action. Linked robots then restrict searches and work to the painted zone.

buildcraftfactory/item/water_gel: Draining an ocean is effective, but sometimes turning the surface into something solid is the more entertaining solution.
The Water Gelifier converts connected source water and aquatic plants into temporary Water Gel.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Check the Recipes and Usages sections together before crafting in bulk; this item may be an intermediate for several later machines.

Use the item while pointing at water. The first gel block is placed at the targeted water position and begins spreading through neighbouring source water and supported aquatic plants. Water Gel advances through random ticks, so the randomTickSpeed gamerule directly affects how quickly it spreads and matures. While a non-spreading gel stage is still touching neighbouring water it does not advance toward final solidification; once that surrounding water is gone, later random ticks can finish the process.

Only fully solidified Water Gel drops Gelled Water when broken. Earlier spreading or gelling stages do not provide the harvest item. The process is intended for controlled water removal and temporary construction, so test it on a small pool before applying it to an ocean.
buildcraftfactory/item/gel: It looks like water, feels rather less like water and no longer behaves like water at all.
Gelled Water is the solid material recovered from Water Gel.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Check the Recipes and Usages sections together before crafting in bulk; this item may be an intermediate for several later machines.
Use a Water Gelifier on source water and wait for the spreading gel to solidify. Breaking the completed gel yields Gelled Water.
buildcraftsilicon/block/laser: Some recipes require precision that a furnace, crafting grid and optimistic hammer cannot provide.
A Laser converts MJ into laser power for nearby compatible BuildCraft tables.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Several Lasers can work on one compatible table. Add them gradually and watch the table buffer so extra laser power is not built where it provides no benefit.

Place Lasers within six blocks of an Assembly, Charging, Integration, Advanced Crafting or Programming Table and supply the Lasers with MJ. Each Laser automatically searches for a compatible table that currently requests power.

A Laser can transfer up to 6.4 MJ per tick. Multiple Lasers may work on the same table, and their beams move as table demand changes.
buildcraftsilicon/block/assembly_table: Redstone and diamonds are useful ingredients, but some components require a much more precise arrangement of energy.
The Assembly Table uses laser power to manufacture BuildCraft components and pluggables.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Select only the recipes that should run automatically. Leaving unrelated recipes enabled can consume shared ingredients when several outputs are possible.

Insert the required ingredients and select one or more available assembly recipes. Nearby powered Lasers fill the selected recipe's energy requirement. When complete, the output is placed in the table or offered to adjacent inventories and pipes.

Several selected recipes may be cycled automatically when their ingredients are available. The table stores partial laser progress, so interrupted work can continue later.
buildcraftsilicon/block/charging_table: A portable machine without energy is merely a decorative machine that is inconvenient to carry.
The Charging Table uses MJ to charge Forge Energy items.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Use filtered input and output inventories around the Charging Table so charged and uncharged items cannot circulate through the same loop indefinitely.

Place a chargeable item in the single slot. Supply MJ directly or with nearby Lasers; the table transfers whole energy units into items exposing the Forge Energy capability.

The table requests only the amount the item can still accept and stops when the item is full. Items that cannot receive energy are rejected.
buildcraftsilicon/block/integration_tabl: Some machines are built in one piece. Others become useful only after the important piece is installed.
The Integration Table installs compatible upgrades or components into a target item using laser power.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Prepare the exact gate, board or robot variant before insertion. Integration recipes often preserve or alter item data that is easier to verify before automation.

Place the target item in the centre slot and the required components in the surrounding slots. If a registered integration recipe matches, nearby Lasers provide its required energy and the finished item appears in the output.

A major Robotics use is installing a programmed Redstone Board into an empty Robot. That operation requires 5,000 MJ.
buildcraftsilicon/block/advanced_craftin: Repeating the same crafting recipe is not difficult, but it is exactly the sort of work a machine should be doing instead.
The Advanced Crafting Table automatically repeats a configured crafting recipe using supplied materials and MJ.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Keep a buffer of each ingredient and extract completed results separately. Recirculating outputs into the ingredient side can block complex recipes.

Arrange the desired recipe in the phantom 3 by 3 blueprint grid, then supply matching ingredients to the material inventory. The table crafts the result into its output inventory whenever the recipe is valid and enough space is available. The Recipe Book can fill the phantom grid directly without consuming ingredients.

If several recipes match the same phantom grid, left-click the result preview for the next recipe or right-click for the previous one; the choice is saved.

Each operation requests 500 MJ. The table can receive MJ directly and also participates in the laser-table system.
buildcraftsilicon/block/programming_tabl: A blank board contains many possibilities and absolutely no useful instructions.
The Programming Table writes a selected robot career onto a blank Redstone Board using laser power.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Program commonly used boards in batches and label their storage. Career boards can look similar until installed in a robot.

Insert a blank Redstone Board, choose a career from the available options and power nearby Lasers. The table outputs a programmed board when the career's energy cost is reached.

Options are ordered by energy cost and name. Basic logistics careers cost 800 MJ; common work careers 3,200 MJ; advanced careers 12,800 MJ; and Builder costs 51,200 MJ.
buildcraftsilicon/item/redstone_crystal: Ordinary redstone dust is energetic, but a crystal is much easier to fit into precision machinery.

<bold>Hint:</bold> Check both recipes and usages before mass-producing this component. Silicon parts are often shared by several machines, gates and robot upgrades.
Produce Redstone Crystals in an Assembly Table with the ingredients shown by the recipe display. They are used in laser machinery, gates and other high-tier components.
buildcraftsilicon/item/gate_copier: A complicated Gate program is much easier to duplicate than to remember perfectly sixteen times.

<bold>Hint:</bold> Keep one verified gate as the master and copy from it. This avoids propagating experimental settings through an entire pipe network.

Use the copier on a configured Gate to store its trigger, action, connection and parameter data. Use the filled copier on another compatible Gate to copy the stored program.

Sneak-right-click in the air to clear the stored data. The item model and tooltip indicate whether a program is currently stored.

<bold>Hint:</bold> Use one wooden extraction connection per intended source and avoid closed loops. Verify the source can safely provide the requested MJ rate.

Its default transfer limit is 16 MJ per tick. Wooden Power Pipes do not connect directly to another wooden extraction pipe.

Power entering a junction is distributed proportionally among requesting outputs. A section accepts no more than its current free capacity, and the network preserves unaccepted energy instead of duplicating or discarding it during normal transfer.

Use Pipe Plugs or paint neighbouring pipes different colours to prevent unwanted connections. Power-pipe limits are configured when the network changes and are restored after loading a world.

The guide uses per-tick rates. Live BuildCraft displays can show the equivalent per-second value when the Core time-gap setting is set to seconds.

<bold>Hint:</bold> Check the Recipes and Usages sections together before crafting in bulk; this item may be an intermediate for several later machines.
