buildcrafttransport/block/filtered_buffe: A buffer is most helpful when it knows which items are actually welcome inside it.
The Filtered Buffer is a nine-slot inventory whose real slots are controlled by matching phantom filters.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Use the Filtered Buffer between fast pipes and slower machines. It smooths bursts and gives filters a stable inventory to work against.

Configure the nine phantom filter slots in the interface. Each matching real inventory slot accepts only the item selected by its filter. Pipes and other item handlers can insert into or extract from the real inventory through the exposed item capability.

Use the buffer between sorting stages to reserve separate storage positions for different items and to stop unrelated stacks from entering the line.
buildcraftenergy/item/oil: A dark liquid bubbling out of the ground is either a valuable energy resource or a very expensive environmental problem.
Oil is the naturally generated starting material for BuildCraft's fuel-processing chain.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Keep raw Oil in its own tank and leave room for intermediate products before starting an automated refinery.
Oil deposits generate in the world and can be collected with Buckets, a Pump or other compatible fluid handlers. Store it in Tanks and move it with Fluid Pipes.

Cool Oil is a dirty Combustion Engine fuel producing 3 MJ/t and Residue. Refining it is normally more valuable.

The Distiller uses the current temperature to choose a route: Cool Oil separates into Gaseous Fuel and Heavy Oil; Hot Oil separates into Mixed Light Fuel and Dense Oil; Searing Oil separates into Distilled Oil and Residue.
buildcraftenergy/item/oil_residue: Every elegant refining chain eventually produces something sticky that nobody wanted to store.
Residue is the heavy by-product of dirty fuels and several high-temperature distillation routes.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Residue is a real output, not waste to ignore. Provide a dedicated tank or controlled disposal route so refining cannot stop.

Crude Oil, Heavy Oil and Dense Oil produce Residue while burning in a Combustion Engine. It is also the liquid output of several Searing distillation recipes.

Residue is not registered as a Combustion Engine fuel. Drain it from engines and machines with Fluid Pipes or containers so residue tanks do not become blocked.

Like the other BuildCraft oil products, Residue has Cool, Hot and Searing states and can exchange heat in a Heat Exchanger. It is primarily a by-product and transportable process fluid in the current project.
buildcraftenergy/item/oil_heavy: The lighter fractions have left. What remains is still energetic, but considerably less cooperative.
Heavy Oil is a dirty intermediate fuel produced by distilling Cool Oil.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Label Heavy Oil lines clearly and keep them separate from fuels; intermediate fluids may look similar in pipes and tanks.
Heavy Oil burns in a Combustion Engine at 2 MJ/t and produces Residue. It is usable directly, but further refining yields cleaner products.

Hot Heavy Oil distils into Light Fuel and Dense Oil. Searing Heavy Oil distils into Mixed Heavy Fuel and Residue. Use a Heat Exchanger to select the required temperature before sending it to the Distiller.
buildcraftenergy/item/oil_dense: Dense Oil contains the part of the original mixture that strongly objects to moving quickly through machinery.
Dense Oil is a dirty intermediate fuel obtained from Hot Oil or Hot Distilled Oil.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Store Dense Oil separately until the next processing step is ready. Feeding it into the wrong temperature stage wastes refinery capacity.
Dense Oil burns at 4 MJ/t in a Combustion Engine and produces Residue. Its higher output is useful when immediate power is more important than clean operation.
Heat Dense Oil to the Searing state and distil it to separate Dense Fuel from Residue. This is the final refining step for its branch of the processing chain.
buildcraftenergy/item/oil_distilled: The first pass removed the worst impurities. Several useful fractions are still sharing the same tank.
Distilled Oil is a clean-burning intermediate containing gaseous, light and dense fuel fractions.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Distilled Oil is an intermediate product. Buffer it so the upstream Distiller can continue while downstream cooling or refining pauses.
Distilled Oil burns without residue at 1 MJ/t. Its direct output is modest, but it is a flexible feedstock for further separation.

Cool Distilled Oil distils into Gaseous Fuel and Mixed Heavy Fuel. Hot Distilled Oil distils into Mixed Light Fuel and Dense Fuel. Change its temperature in a Heat Exchanger before choosing the next route.
buildcraftenergy/item/fuel_gaseous: The lightest fraction is eager to leave both the Distiller and any poorly planned pipe network.
Gaseous Fuel is the highest-output refined Combustion Engine fuel, producing 8 MJ/t without residue.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Reserve high-value fuel for engines that can use it efficiently and provide automatic shutdown when the consumer stops.

Gaseous Fuel is the top output of distilling Cool Oil, Cool Distilled Oil or Cool Mixed Light Fuel. It has Cool, Hot and Searing forms for transport through the Heat Exchanger, although it does not require further distillation.

Use it when a machine needs the largest instantaneous output from one Combustion Engine. High output also adds heat quickly, so maintain a reliable coolant supply and an MJ consumer that can accept the generated power.
buildcraftenergy/item/fuel_light: Light Fuel is the sensible middle ground between a short energetic burst and a barrel that lasts all week.
Light Fuel is a clean refined fuel producing 6 MJ/t in a Combustion Engine.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Use separate fuel tanks for each grade. This makes engine runtime and refinery throughput easier to compare.
Distil Cool Mixed Light Fuel, Hot Heavy Oil or Hot Mixed Heavy Fuel to obtain Light Fuel. It does not produce Residue when burned.
Light Fuel combines high output with clean operation. Keep the engine cooled and ensure the connected MJ network can accept 6 MJ every tick.
buildcraftenergy/item/fuel_dense: Dense Fuel values endurance over enthusiasm and is quite content to keep an engine working for a long time.
Dense Fuel is a clean refined fuel producing 4 MJ/t with a long burn duration.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Dense Fuel is valuable enough to justify buffered delivery and an engine shutdown trigger before unattended operation.
Hot Distilled Oil, Hot Mixed Heavy Fuel and Searing Dense Oil can produce Dense Fuel. The Dense Oil route also separates Residue as its second output.
Dense Fuel burns without creating residue. Its moderate output and high total energy make it well suited to sustained machinery rather than short peak loads.
buildcraftenergy/item/fuel_mixed_light: Two useful fuels are sharing one tank. The Distiller can settle the ownership dispute.
Mixed Light Fuel is a clean intermediate and a usable 3 MJ/t Combustion Engine fuel.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Treat mixed fuels as distinct products and avoid reconnecting them to intermediate-oil lines.
Hot Oil and Hot Distilled Oil produce Mixed Light Fuel as their gaseous output. It contains gaseous and light fuel fractions.
Distil Cool Mixed Light Fuel to separate Gaseous Fuel and Light Fuel. It may also be burned directly without producing Residue.
buildcraftenergy/item/fuel_mixed_heavy: Light and dense fuel are compatible tank-mates, but separating them makes their different strengths easier to use.
Mixed Heavy Fuel is a clean intermediate and a usable 5 MJ/t Combustion Engine fuel.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Buffer heavy mixed fuel close to its consumers, but keep the main refinery outputs separated for easier troubleshooting.
Cool Distilled Oil and Searing Heavy Oil can produce Mixed Heavy Fuel. It contains light and dense fuel fractions.

buildcraftcompat/pipe/propolis_item: Sorting bees by colour was never going to be precise enough for a serious apiary.
The Apiarist's Pipe is a Forestry compatibility item pipe that routes genetic items with a separate filter for every side.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Use an Apiarist's Pipe at a dedicated bee-processing junction. Keep a normal overflow route so unexpected bee types do not block the network.

Open the pipe to configure each output face. Forestry filter rules can match genetic items by species, species family and life stage. Up to three selected species can be assigned to a side, and each entry may be enabled or disabled independently.

Items are routed through the first compatible output according to the configured Forestry rules. Outputs without an active matching rule do not claim the genetic item. The pipe can be painted and connected like other BuildCraft item pipes.

This page is loaded only when Forestry is installed and the compatibility item is registered.
buildcraftenergy/block/engine_fe: Some factories arrive with FE already flowing through the walls. There is no requirement that BuildCraft pretend not to notice.
The FE Engine consumes Forge Energy, converts it into MJ and behaves as a directional BuildCraft engine.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Use the FE Engine when an FE network should power an MJ-only BuildCraft network without enabling automatic conversion for every ordinary machine.

The engine accepts FE into a 10,000 FE input buffer and produces 4 MJ/t by default. At the default 1 MJ = 10 FE ratio that consumes up to 40 FE/t. Generated MJ is held in the normal 1,000 MJ engine buffer and sent through the engine output face. The converter works even when Core power mode is MJ_ONLY.

The GUI has four upgrade slots and accepts one supported gear per slot. Each Iron Gear adds 2 MJ/t; each Gold Gear adds 3 MJ/t. The FE consumption rate follows the configured MJ/FE ratio, so changing power.mjPerFe changes the FE cost of the same MJ output.

Supply a redstone signal and rotate the engine so its moving end faces the MJ consumer or Power Pipe. If the MJ buffer cannot accept another conversion pulse, the engine waits instead of consuming FE for power it cannot store. Like other non-Redstone engines it has heat and should not be left permanently blocked under load.
buildcraftenergy/block/mj_dynamo: Sometimes the machine on the other end speaks FE, while the rest of the factory has already committed to MJ.
The MJ Dynamo consumes BuildCraft MJ and produces Forge Energy through its directional output face.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Point the Dynamo directly at an FE consumer or an FE extraction/network arrangement, and feed MJ into one of its other faces. This makes the conversion boundary obvious.

The Dynamo stores up to 1,000 MJ and up to 10,000 FE. Its base conversion rate is 4 MJ/t worth of energy, which is 40 FE/t at the default 1 MJ = 10 FE ratio. MJ enters on non-output faces; FE leaves through the facing/output side. The dedicated converter works even when Core power mode is MJ_ONLY.

The four upgrade slots use the same rules as the FE Engine: each Iron Gear adds 2 MJ/t of conversion capacity and each Gold Gear adds 3 MJ/t. The actual FE/t result follows the configured MJ/FE ratio.

A redstone signal enables conversion. The Dynamo does not consume MJ for a pulse that would fill or overflow its FE buffer. When disabled, its stored FE slowly self-discharges by 1 FE per tick, matching the restored BuildCraft 8 converter behaviour. Rotate it with a Wrench to choose the FE output face.

The Wooden FE Pipe extracts FE from an adjacent energy source and injects it into the FE-pipe network.
<bold>Hint:</bold> Put extraction pipes only on actual FE providers and size the next segment for the same load. A fast source cannot push through a slower downstream bottleneck.

Its default transfer limit is 160 FE/t. FE pipe rates are derived from pipes.baseFeRate, which defaults to 40 FE/t, so a pack can scale the whole family without changing its tier relationships. Like other wooden energy extraction pipes, it does not connect directly to another wooden FE extraction pipe. FE Pipes connect to compatible FE energy capabilities, request only energy the network can use and preserve unaccepted energy instead of duplicating it. They are dedicated FE transport and remain available in MJ_ONLY mode. Pipe holders can also be waterlogged in current Minecraft versions.
